summary.intent: Execute Phase 41 (Package and App Versioning and Release Cycles) using GSD wave-based parallel execution, completing all 5 plans across 4 waves.
summary.outcome: Wave 1 (41-01) and Wave 2 (41-02, 41-04) were completed after significant worktree branch management issues and lint fixes; Wave 3 and Wave 4 remain unexecuted. STATE.md was also cleaned up (performance metrics table reformatted, stale open concerns removed).

repo: Monorepo has 15 packages configured for independent versioning via release-please; root extra-files removed but desktop extra-files retained.
61 GitHub release labels are required for the per-package release workflow and must be created via script.
macOS ships with bash 3.2 which does not support `declare -A` associative arrays; scripts targeting local dev or CI must use bash 3.2-compatible alternatives.
Pre-commit hooks run lint-staged on commit; ESLint rule for unused vars is `@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars` (not `no-unused-vars`).
Staging deploy infrastructure uses `staging-*` tag pattern with date-based tags (`staging-YYYYMMDD-release-N`) and triple-tagged Docker images.
GSD executor agents spawn worktrees branched from main HEAD, not from the current feature branch — merging worktrees back requires cherry-pick, not fast-forward merge.
STATE.md performance metrics table had a mixed format (old 5-column vs new 4-column `Phase XX PYY` format); now normalized to 4-column throughout.
Open Concerns in STATE.md had 3 fully resolved items: rootFolderKey migration complete (DB columns dropped), BYO-IPFS auth implemented as encrypted IPNS entry, Kubo already at v0.40.0.

code.finding: Agent-generated script had dead code: `maxBump` function defined but never called, `directBumps` and `computedLabelSet` assigned but never read. These were removed to pass lint.

workflow: lint-staged runs a stash-restore cycle during commit that clobbers in-place edits to already-staged files — edits must be made before staging, or files must be re-staged after editing.
529 API overload errors introduced ~25 min of dead wall-clock time during Wave 1 despite only ~4 min of actual agent work; unavoidable but worth accounting for in time estimates.
When multiple GSD agents update STATE.md in parallel worktrees, merging them back creates conflicts that must be resolved manually.

The `cd` to a worktree path persists across tool calls — the orchestrator's working directory can silently drift into a worktree branch, masking that commits aren't landing on the intended feature branch.

friction: 529 API overload errors caused ~25 minutes of retry-backoff dead time during Wave 1 agent execution.
GSD executor worktrees branch from main, not from the feature branch — `git merge worktree-branch` returned 'Already up to date' silently, requiring cherry-pick recovery.
Orchestrator's working directory drifted to a worktree branch mid-session, causing confusion about which branch commits were landing on.
lint-staged stash-restore cycle clobbered edits to staged files multiple times, requiring iterative approaches (eslint-disable comment → remove dead code entirely).
ESLint rule name mismatch: initial `eslint-disable no-unused-vars` comment had no effect; correct rule is `@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars`.
First commit attempt for Wave 2 merge failed due to non-conventional commit message format.
Multi-agent STATE.md conflicts required manual resolution during worktree integration.
open_items: Wave 3 (41-03: post-merge release-as injection) not yet executed.
Wave 4 (41-05: batched releases + desktop updater workflow) not yet executed.
Stashed STATE.md changes (performance metrics table reformatting) need to be verified as correctly applied after the wave 2 merge resolution.
6 remaining LOW-priority tech debt items from M2 audit (partially outdated concern retained in STATE.md).
Subfolder recovery limitation due to IPNS DHT propagation is architectural and tracked as an open concern — not a bug to fix but worth revisiting if DHT reliability improves.
